purpose: Candidate V2 routing rules: for every eligible canonical interest, decide a default non-human-first protagonist type and an object-first readiness status, based only on catalog semantics (archetype/category/id), never on generated-image visual review. V1 (global_style_v1.json, buildPromptV1.js, production_queue_v1.json) is read-only input and is never modified by this spec or its compiler. This file is authoritative input for src/objectFirstV2Router.js, src/compileObjectFirstPromptV2.js, and src/auditObjectFirstV2.js.
philosophy: Default assumption is non-human-first: find an object/environment/animal/machine/aftermath/miniature/symbolic storytelling solution before ever treating a hobby as human-required. A hobby must NOT be classified human_exception_candidate merely because people commonly perform it in real life. Uncertain cases route to review_required, not to a human-led default lane. Every archetype_defaults entry carries an explicit `confidence` value so a reader can distinguish 'validated by a real round' from 'extrapolated with high confidence' from 'a new scene grammar written this round, not yet visually tested' - accuracy is prioritized over artificially minimizing the review_required count.
changelog_v2_1: Part B of the 2026-09-25 compiler task rerouted 6 of the 7 previously review_required archetypes (professional_world, music_listening, campus_activity, shared_workspace, campaign_planning, legal_practice) to containment_required using new, explicit positive scene grammars (see structural_containment_rules_v2.json's new rules). community_gathering was also rerouted but flagged confidence=weak_extrapolation per the task's own instruction that this specific archetype is the hardest case and should not be forced if genuinely weak. Also fixed the human_exception_keyword_scan from naive substring matching to token-aware matching plus an explicit known_false_positive_ids exclusion list for remaining lexical ambiguity (see human_exception_keyword_scan below).

evidence_rounds.round4_note: Round 4 images were generated with structural containment prompts and remained pending external visual QA (ChatGPT) at the time this V2 architecture was written. This audit treats the round-3-to-round-4 prompt REDESIGN itself (not yet a confirmed visual pass) as the evidence that structural containment is the correct mechanism; the containment rules below are written from that redesign, not from an assumed Round 4 pass/fail outcome.

solo_action.rationale: Validated directly: sports.running (round 3->4) required aftermath staging (shoes at rest, footprints, stopwatch) rather than shoes mid-run to avoid legs appearing.

vertical_adventure.rationale: Not yet directly tested. Extrapolated from solo_action/outdoor_motion: gear (harness, chalk dust, rope) at rest on an empty wall/route can carry the same aftermath storytelling.

group_play.rationale: Validated directly: gaming.board (round 3->4) required a private, empty game room instead of a social/cafe venue to stop background people appearing.

food_hero.rationale: Archetype's own V1 composition language already makes the food itself the hero; validated repeatedly (food.baking, food.dish.bun_cha) with no containment redesign needed beyond the baseline no-human directive.

drink_ritual.rationale: Not directly tested under this name, but food.coffee (round 2) is semantically identical and needed an empty/private venue treatment to avoid background cafe patrons.

travel_vista.rationale: Validated directly: travel.roadtrip (round 3) required an empty vehicle interior (no driver/passenger silhouette) alongside the environment.

urban_discovery.rationale: Not yet tested. Environment-led by its own V1 description; treated as a lower-confidence sibling of travel_vista pending a dedicated test.

performance.rationale: Validated directly: music.piano (round 3) worked cleanly by making the instrument itself the hero with no performer.

creative_studio.rationale: Validated indirectly via crafts.pottery_wheel (round 1) and the general craft/process family; the making process reads through material/tool state rather than hands.

lens_perspective.rationale: Validated directly: photography.general (round 3) was one of the cleanest results in the entire program using the camera/lens itself as hero.

tech_workspace.rationale: Validated as the hardest case: technology.ai failed severely in round 3 (human hands/arms/torso dominated the frame) specifically because the scene was built around a device operator; round 4 redesigned it as a pure abstract network/hardware metaphor with no operator.

collection_object_hero.rationale: Archetype's own V1 composition language is already object-hero-first; requires no containment redesign beyond the baseline no-human directive.

calm_wellness.rationale: Not yet tested. Environment/equipment-led by nature (mat, candle, cushion); treated as containment_required by extrapolation, not review, since no interpersonal content is semantically required.

nature_immersion.rationale: Validated directly: outdoors.camping (round 2) worked cleanly using tent/fire/gear with a genuinely empty campsite.

story_culture.rationale: Validated as a hard case: media.movies failed in round 3 (human silhouette rendered ON the screen); round 4 redesigned the rule to require non-human screen content (galaxy/ocean/landscape/abstract lights) plus a genuinely empty auditorium.

learning_exploration.rationale: Not yet tested under this archetype name, but its own V1 recognition language already anchors on 'concrete source, specimen, object' rather than requiring a visible learner; extrapolated from reading_world's validated pattern.

companion_bond.rationale: Validated directly: pets.dogs (round 3) worked well with a real-dog protagonist, but leaked small background human silhouettes through a street-facing window; round 4 redesigned the environment to be fully private (fenced garden or interior with a garden/sky-only window).

professional_world.rationale: Rerouted from review_required in v2.1: the profession's own material world (field-specific tools, documents, equipment, outputs of work) is a plausible non-human hero, per the archetype's own V1 language already favoring a physical tool/task over generic office scenery. Not yet visually tested.

journey_machine.rationale: Validated directly: travel.roadtrip's vehicle-as-hero treatment (round 3) generalizes cleanly to any single-vehicle/machine hobby.

music_listening.rationale: Rerouted from review_required in v2.1: the listening ritual can plausibly be carried by audio equipment and acoustic environment alone (headphones, turntable, listening room) without a listener present. Distinct from the validated performance/instrument case. Not yet visually tested.

reading_world.rationale: Validated directly: books.reading (round 2) worked cleanly with an open book as hero and no reader.

strategy_table.rationale: Extrapolated directly from group_play's validated gaming.board result; near-identical composition language (tabletop, pieces, cards).

digital_play.rationale: Not tested, but the archetype's own V1 language already forbids a front-facing gameplay screen and already favors the physical controller/device as recognition cue, making an object-first treatment a small, low-risk extension.

fitness_training.rationale: Extrapolated directly from sports.running and sports.basketball's validated aftermath/in-flight staging.

water_outdoors.rationale: Validated as a hard case: outdoors.swimming leaked a human foot/ankle in round 3 even with an 'aftermath splash' framing; round 4 tightened the rule to forbid any narrative implying a currently- or just-departed swimmer, using only static empty-lane cues instead.

outdoor_motion.rationale: Extrapolated directly from sports.running's validated aftermath treatment; outdoors.mountain_biking (round 1) also passed cleanly using a similar object/gear-led approach.

home_lifestyle.rationale: Validated directly: lifestyle.gardening (round 3) and lifestyle.home_decor (round 2) both worked cleanly with no person present.

food_exploration.rationale: Validated directly: food.dish.bun_cha (rounds 1-2) needed an explicitly empty street/restaurant background to stop diners appearing.

campus_activity.rationale: Rerouted from review_required in v2.1: the specific campus environment, activity equipment, and event materials are a plausible non-human hero. Not yet visually tested.

community_gathering.rationale: Rerouted from review_required in v2.1, but explicitly flagged as the lowest-confidence reroute in the whole set. Uses a 'traces of community' grammar (prepared table, arranged chairs, communal objects, before/after staging) since the archetype's semantic core is interpersonal connection, which is the hardest case to fully substitute. Individual ids within this archetype that still read as weak after a future visual test should be moved back to review_required rather than kept here by default.

wellness_experience.rationale: Not tested directly under this archetype, but is a close sibling of calm_wellness and wellness.cold_plunge/wellness.tai_chi (validated in earlier V1 recipe-fix rounds, pre-object-first) show the environment/equipment already carries most of the recognition.

creator_workflow.rationale: Not tested directly, but shares technology.ai's core risk (device-operator cliche); routed to the same containment rule as a precaution.

shared_workspace.rationale: Rerouted from review_required in v2.1: multiple distinct, personalized desks shown side by side can plausibly communicate 'multiple independent workers' through belongings rather than bodies. Not yet visually tested - this is one of the harder reroutes since an empty-desks scene risks reading as simply unoccupied.

campaign_planning.rationale: Rerouted from review_required in v2.1: campaign materials (mockups, swatches, layout pieces) arranged on a table are a plausible non-human hero. Not yet visually tested.

legal_practice.rationale: Rerouted from review_required in v2.1: case files, evidence folders, and courtroom/office architecture are a plausible non-human hero, with a restrained scales-of-justice detail as supporting texture only. Not yet visually tested.

aviation_world.rationale: Extrapolated directly from journey_machine's validated vehicle-as-hero pattern; aircraft is already the archetype's own V1-mandated dominant hero object.

physical_prototype.rationale: Not tested, but the archetype's own V1 language already forbids all screens and favors the prototype/mechanism itself; only the 'hands adjusting it' language needs removing, a small delta from the validated technology.ai fix.

screenless_broadcast.rationale: Not tested, but the archetype is already screen-free by design; recognition can plausibly shift to the studio equipment (mic, light stand, camera rig) alone with no performer.

screenless_pc_play.rationale: Not tested, but already screen-free by design; recognition can plausibly shift to the desktop tower/keyboard/headphones as a still-life setup with a freshly-left seat.

id_prefix_overrides.rationale: Explicit id-level override ensuring every pets.* hobby (not only pets.dogs, which was the one directly tested) inherits the validated real-animal-protagonist + private-environment pattern, per the explicit animal carve-out (zero-HUMANS rule, not zero-living-beings).
Validated directly: collecting.stamps (round 1) passed cleanly with no containment redesign needed; collecting.* is inherently object-hero-first.

Added during the 2026-09-25 final zero-cost gate's Part-7 community_gathering review: the archetype default's community_gathering_traces grammar (shared table, chairs, food, decorations) produces genuine nonsense for a car meet, whose actual shared object is the vehicles themselves. This override routes to the new community_gathering_vehicles rule instead. Still weak_extrapolation - not visually tested.

Added during the 2026-09-25 final zero-cost gate's Part-7 community_gathering review: the archetype default's community_gathering_traces grammar (a 'warmly prepared for togetherness' communal table) tonally mismatches a repair workshop, whose identity is tools/materials/craft-in-progress, not a social table. This override routes to generic_structural_containment instead, which already reads correctly for a workshop-style scene (arranged tools, natural wear, an activity mid-progress). Still weak_extrapolation - not visually tested.

human_exception_keyword_scan.purpose: A narrow, conservative mechanism to surface candidates whose id or title suggests the hobby's identity might be inseparable from a visible human body/identity being displayed or performing directly to an audience. Every match is then programmatically CHALLENGED against object/aftermath/environment/animal/machine/miniature/symbolic alternatives before being accepted as a true human_exception_candidate; matches are downgraded to containment_required whenever a plausible non-human alternative exists. This mechanism is text-only and does not consult any generated image.
human_exception_keyword_scan.matching_method_v2_1: Token-aware matching (fixed in v2.1, was naive substring matching in v2.0). The id and title are tokenized on non-alphanumeric boundaries (so 'crafts.model_building' -> ['crafts','model','building'], 'technology.3d_modeling' -> ['technology','3d','modeling']). A single-word pattern (e.g. 'model') matches only an EXACT token, not a substring of a longer word - this alone fixed 'technology.3d_modeling' (token is 'modeling', not 'model'), 'transport.modelrailways' (token is 'modelrailways', not 'model'), 'learning.self_improvement' and 'lifestyle.home_improvement' (token is 'improvement', not 'improv'), and 'outdoors.dragon_boat'/'sports.dragon_boat_racing' (token is 'dragon', not 'drag'). A multi-word pattern (e.g. 'stand_up') matches only that exact consecutive token sequence. Token matching alone cannot resolve genuine lexical ambiguity where the whole word really is a token but means something unrelated (e.g. 'model' the noun for a scale model, not a fashion model) - those remaining cases are handled by the explicit known_false_positive_ids exclusion list below, each with a written reason.

challenge_alternatives.model: garment/clothing displayed on a mannequin, hanger, or dress form as the object hero (no visible face)
challenge_alternatives.pageant: crown/sash/staging displayed on an empty pedestal as the object hero
challenge_alternatives.runway: an empty runway/catwalk environment with garment displays, no walking figure
challenge_alternatives.public_speaking: a podium with a microphone and an empty audience of seats, aftermath staging (papers left on the podium)
challenge_alternatives.debate: a debate table/podium arrangement with name-cards and an empty gallery, aftermath staging
challenge_alternatives.stand_up: a microphone stand under a spotlight with an empty stool, aftermath staging (already validated pattern for arts.comedy_writing's notebook/mic-stand treatment)
challenge_alternatives.improv: a bare stage with a single prop and a spotlight, no performer
challenge_alternatives.beauty_queen: sash/crown/staging on an empty pedestal as the object hero
challenge_alternatives.drag: costume/wig/makeup vanity display as the object hero, no face
challenge_alternatives.cosplay_performance: costume on a mannequin/display form as the object hero, no wearer

known_false_positive_ids.crafts.model_building: 'model' here means a scale/toy model (model building as a craft hobby), not fashion modeling. Token 'model' is literally present but the meaning is unrelated to the human-display concern this scan targets.
known_false_positive_ids.crafts.model_kit_building: Same as crafts.model_building - scale model kit assembly, not fashion modeling.
known_false_positive_ids.learning.model_united_nations: 'Model' here means a simulation exercise (Model UN), not fashion modeling.
known_false_positive_ids.outdoors.stand_up_paddleboarding: 'stand_up' here is the watersport (stand-up paddleboarding), not stand-up comedy. The consecutive token sequence 'stand','up' is a genuine but unrelated collision that token matching alone cannot resolve.
known_false_positive_ids.transport.modelrailways: The id itself has no separator ('modelrailways' is one token, already unambiguous), but its title 'Model Railways' contains 'Model' as its own word, so the title-side scan still matches the standalone token 'model'. Same scale/toy-model meaning as crafts.model_building, not fashion modeling.

human_exception_keyword_scan.irreducible_human_ids_note: This allowlist is intentionally empty. Every keyword-scan match found in the real 2210-row catalog (after the v2.1 token-matching fix and known_false_positive_ids exclusion) was challenged and downgraded to containment_required using the alternative above; see the audit's human_exception_candidates output for the exact ids this ran against. If a future review finds a genuine case where no non-human alternative is plausible, it should be added here explicitly with a written rationale, never inferred automatically.

quarantine_note: Quarantined ids (from specs/generation_guardrails_v1.json's quarantined map, currently sports.american_football and technology.robotics) are routed to object_first_status=excluded_quarantined with protagonist_type=null and are excluded from every V2 distribution/aggregate. This spec never modifies the quarantine file.
